what: Enbridge moves energy through pipelines. Its Mainline system carries the largest volume of Canadian crude oil into the United States, and it also owns North American gas pipelines, gas utilities serving millions of customers, and renewable power.
customers: Oil producers in Alberta, refiners in the US Midwest and Gulf Coast, gas shippers, and household gas customers in Ontario and three US states.
money: the Mainline crude oil system and related pipelines
regulated gas utilities in Ontario and the United States
moat: Pipeline corridors that would be nearly impossible to permit today, with capacity contracted under long-term, mostly regulated terms.
risks: Debt of about $80 billion is very large and interest-rate sensitive
Return on invested capital is low at around 5%
New pipeline projects face long regulatory and legal challenges
It issues shares and debt regularly to fund growth
opportunities: Revenue grew about 28% last year after acquiring three US gas utilities
About 98% of cash flow comes from regulated or contracted sources
A dividend yield near 6% raised for three decades running
watch: Distributable cash flow per share and the debt-to-EBITDA ratio.
